result.markdown:
# Nationwide Data Slowdown and Traffic Dip

- **Classification:** incident
- **Root cause:** bad_change at `CORE-UPF-01`
- **Confidence:** medium (Timing directly follows core software patches affecting DNS, UPF, and AMF, matching the nationwide degradation pattern.)
- **Impact:** 2026-09-03 13:15 to 2026-09-03 15:45
- **Cause time:** 2026-09-03 12:16
- **Affected:** CORE-DNS-01, CORE-UPF-01, CORE-AMF-01

## Summary

Software upgrades on core network nodes introduced processing inefficiencies resulting in nationwide traffic dips and latency spikes.

Nationwide traffic, DNS query success, and UPF throughput dropped while latency spiked.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-03 12:14: Software upgrade applied on CORE-DNS-01. [CHG-2026-0003]
- 2026-09-03 12:16: Software upgrade applied on CORE-UPF-01. [CHG-2026-0004]
- 2026-09-03 12:17: Software upgrade applied on CORE-AMF-01. [CHG-2026-0005]
- 2026-09-03 13:15: Nationwide alert ALR-0001 began for traffic, DNS, and UPF throughput drop. [T1, ALR-0001]
- 2026-09-03 13:15: National dl_volume_mb fell below baseline. [T2]
- 2026-09-03 15:45: Nationwide degradation alert ALR-0001 ended. [ALR-0001]

## Evidence

- Alert ALR-0001 shows nationwide traffic, DNS query success, and UPF throughput drops from 13:15 to 15:45. [T1, ALR-0001]
- National dl_volume_mb showed deviation below baseline starting at 13:15. [T2]
- Software patch 21.4.2 to 21.4.3 applied to CORE-DNS-01 at 12:14. [CHG-2026-0003]
- Software patch 21.4.2 to 21.4.3 applied to CORE-UPF-01 at 12:16 with service restart. [CHG-2026-0004]
- Software patch 21.4.2 to 21.4.3 applied to CORE-AMF-01 at 12:17. [CHG-2026-0005]
- CORE-UPF-01 experienced a throughput drop anomaly with z -6.2. [ANM-000003]

## Hypotheses

1. **bad_change** at CORE-UPF-01: confirmed. Core software upgrades closely preceded nationwide performance degradation and throughput drops. [CHG-2026-0004, ALR-0001]
2. **planned_maintenance** at S-SAH-001: rejected. Maintenance on S-SAH-001 concluded before the nationwide impact onset time. [MW-0002]

## Ruled out

- MW-0002: Cabinet cleaning and filter replacement at S-SAH-001 completed well before the nationwide impact onset at 13:15.
- CHG-2026-0006: Parameter tuning on S-TUN-014 occurred at 13:30, after the nationwide impact already began.
- CHG-2026-0007: Neighbour list update on S-SAH-011 occurred at 15:48, after the impact window ended.

## Recommended actions

- Review software patch 21.4.3 release notes for potential packet processing regressions.
- Perform post-upgrade stability checks on core UPF and DNS nodes.

## Sources

- `CHG-2026-0003`: software_upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 at 2026-09-03 12:14: Software patch 21.4.2 -> 21.4.3 on CORE-DNS-01 (resolver service restart)
- `CHG-2026-0004`: software_upgrade on CORE-UPF-01 at 2026-09-03 12:16: Software patch 21.4.2 -> 21.4.3 on CORE-UPF-01 (service restart)
- `CHG-2026-0005`: software_upgrade on CORE-AMF-01 at 2026-09-03 12:17: Software patch 21.4.2 -> 21.4.3 on CORE-AMF-01 (service restart)

- `T2`: query_kpis(entity_type=national, metrics=['dl_volume_mb', 'ul_volume_mb', 'latency_ms'], start=2026-09-03 12:00, end=2026-09-03 18:00) -> Deviation in 3 of 3 series. Earliest onset 2026-09-03 13:15: NATIONAL dl_volume_mb below baseline.

confounders.why: Harmless software_upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 completed 56 min before the degradation; the DNS KPIs stayed normal until the onset and the same patch on other core nodes did nothing.

truth.notes: trap=change_on_root_node; CORE-DNS-01 degraded for about 159 min; nationwide latency up, volume down, RRC unaffected. No alarm was raised; the evidence is in core_kpis. Trap: a software upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 itself ran 56 min before the onset, so a hasty investigator blames the change. Settled by: (1) the DNS and RRC KPIs were normal for 56 min after the upgrade, while a configuration change takes effect at once; (2) the same patch under the same ticket went onto CORE-AMF-01 and CORE-UPF-01 at the same time and both stayed healthy; (3) the degradation ended by itself, with no rollback or other change at the recovery.
